name: browserbuddy
help: Share one browser between you and your coding agent. install-host sets up the native-messaging host the extension spawns by default; serve runs the MCP stdio server with the WebSocket hub for builds that use the WebSocket carrier instead.

serve.name: serve
serve.help: Run the MCP stdio server and the WebSocket hub. Only the WebSocket carrier uses this: with the extension's default native transport the browser spawns the host itself (see install-host).

flags.name: port
flags.help: WebSocket hub port on 127.0.0.1. Must match WS_URL in extension/background.js, which only applies when that file sets TRANSPORT to websocket.

flags.name: data-dir
flags.help: Directory for event logs and recorded demonstrations. Defaults to server/data inside the installed package.

install-host.name: install-host
install-host.help: Install the native-messaging host manifest so the browser can spawn the BrowserBuddy host (which serves MCP over loopback HTTP).

flags.name: browser
flags.help: Which browser to install for. "chrome" covers the whole Chromium family.

flags.name: user-data-dir
flags.help: Chrome only: the browser profile directory (--user-data-dir). Defaults to the first Chrome or Chromium profile directory that exists under your home.

flags.name: home
flags.help: Firefox only: the HOME whose .mozilla/native-messaging-hosts receives the manifest. Defaults to your home directory.

flags.name: data-dir
flags.help: Directory the installed host will use for event logs, demonstrations and its endpoint files. Defaults to server/data inside the installed package.
